q: How does account correlation decide which identity an account belongs to when I configure several attribute pairs? What if none matches?
must: pairs are tried one at a time in order and the first matching pair correlates (not an AND of all pairs)
operation is Equals only, case-insensitive by default
fallback: account name compared with the identity name
A: Correlation pairs (identity attribute <-> account attribute, operation Equals/`EQ` only) are evaluated one at a time, in the configured order, and the first pair that matches correlates the account; it is an OR, not an AND of all pairs. Matching is case-insensitive by default (per-assignment `ignoreCase` via the API). Put the most reliable, unique identifier (employee number, immutable ID) first and names last or never. Only searchable identity attributes can be used (identities must be processed first) and account values over 128 characters are not supported. If no configured pair matches, ISC falls back to default correlation: account name compared with the identity `name` (case-insensitive, not configurable). If that also fails the account stays uncorrelated (no access, not governed) until you fix data/config, use a Correlation rule (`accountCorrelationRule`), or correlate manually with the correlation file. Config API: `GET/PUT /sources/v1/{id}/correlation-config` (`attributeAssignments` with `property`, `value`, `operation: EQ`, `ignoreCase`, `matchMode`).
B: Correlation is configured on the source's correlation config (Accounts > Correlation in the UI; GET/PUT /beta/sources/{id}/correlation-config). Each entry pairs an identity attribute with an account attribute (attributeAssignments: property, value/accountAttribute, operation EQ, matchMode). During aggregation ISC evaluates the pairs in order and the account is correlated to the identity on the first pair that yields a unique match; if a pair matches multiple identities it is skipped/treated as ambiguous and the next pair is tried. Matching is generally case-insensitive exact equality; empty account values do not match. If no pair matches (and no Correlation rule assigns one), the account stays uncorrelated. For an authoritative source an uncorrelated account creates a new identity; for a non-authoritative source it stays in the Uncorrelated Accounts list and must be correlated manually (UI or PUT /v3/accounts/{id} with identityId) or by fixing data/config and re-aggregating. A Correlation rule (cloud rule, attached via correlationRule) can replace or complement the attribute pairs.

q: I changed the correlation configuration of a source and re-ran aggregation from the UI, but old accounts are still uncorrelated. Why, and how do I fix it?
must: optimized aggregation skips unchanged accounts and does not re-evaluate correlation
run an aggregation with disableOptimization=true via POST /sources/v1/{id}/load-accounts (API only; UI runs are always optimized)
must_not: says a UI checkbox disables optimization
A: UI-started aggregations are always optimized: accounts whose data did not change since the last aggregation are skipped, and correlation (and manager correlation) is not re-evaluated for them, so old uncorrelated accounts stay uncorrelated. Fix: run one unoptimized aggregation via the API, `POST /sources/v1/{id}/load-accounts` as `multipart/form-data` with field `disableOptimization=true` (applies to that run only); track it with `GET /account-aggregations/v1/{taskId}/status`. If accounts still do not correlate, check that the identity attribute is searchable and populated after identity processing, value formats match (leading zeros, domain prefixes, case), values are unique, and the account attribute is in the account schema. Manually correlated accounts (`manuallyCorrelated=true`) are not changed by unoptimized aggregation. Remaining ones can be correlated with the correlation file (`POST /sources/v1/{id}/load-uncorrelated-accounts`).
B: Normal (optimized/delta) aggregation only reprocesses accounts whose source data changed since the last run, so unchanged accounts are not re-evaluated against the new correlation config and stay uncorrelated. Fix: run an unoptimized aggregation, i.e. disable optimization - in the UI via the aggregation option to 'disable optimization' or via API POST /beta/sources/{sourceId}/load-accounts (or v3 /v2024 equivalent) with form field disableOptimization=true. That forces every account to be reprocessed, including correlation. Also ensure the identity attributes used in correlation are populated (identities refreshed) and values match exactly. Alternatively correlate remaining ones manually or via account PUT with identityId.

q: How does the account delete threshold work, and which aggregations can delete accounts?
must: percentage of the source's accounts (deleteThreshold 0-100)
if exceeded, the delete phase is skipped with a warning
deletes only in full aggregations with account deletion enabled; delta/single-account aggregations do not delete
must_not: says it is an absolute number of accounts
A: The account delete threshold (source setting deleteThreshold, default 10%, configurable in source Account Aggregation settings) protects against mass deletion: if an aggregation would remove more than that percentage of the source's existing accounts, the aggregation is stopped/fails with an error and no accounts are deleted, so a bad feed or empty file cannot wipe accounts and trigger cascading lifecycle changes. Only full account aggregations can delete accounts (accounts missing from the full feed are removed); delta/partial aggregations and single-account aggregations (e.g. reload account) do not delete missing accounts, and entitlement aggregations affect entitlements not accounts. For an intentional large cleanup you temporarily raise the threshold (e.g. PATCH /v3/sources/{id} /deleteThreshold) and rerun, then restore it. Authoritative-source deletions are the most dangerous since they can remove identities.
B: Accounts missing from the source are removed from ISC only if Enable Account Deletion is on, and only by full account aggregations (schedule, Start Aggregation, `POST /sources/v1/{id}/load-accounts`); delta aggregations and single-account reloads (`POST /accounts/v1/{id}/reload`) never delete. The delete threshold (source field `deleteThreshold`, 0-100) is a percentage of the source's accounts: if an aggregation would delete more than that, the delete phase is skipped and a warning is raised (account deletion skipped, threshold exceeded), and the accounts stay until you fix the source or raise the threshold for one run. On small sources the percentage is rounded to whole accounts; if it rounds below one account only a 100% deletion is blocked. Typical value is low (about 10%) so an empty/truncated read (VA problem, wrong base DN, empty file) cannot wipe access. Enable deletion and set the threshold only after the first clean aggregations.

q: In a create profile, my mail field uses a static Velocity value "$uid@corp.com" but mail comes out wrong. uid is generated by Create Unique Account ID further down. What's wrong?
must: fields are computed in list order: uid must be placed before mail
static values can reference earlier fields only (generator patterns cannot reference other fields)
A: Create profile fields are computed top to bottom, so a Static (Velocity) value can only reference fields defined earlier. Because `uid` (generator `Create Unique Account ID`, i.e. transform `{"type":"rule","attributes":{"name":"Create Unique Account ID"}}`) is below `mail`, `$uid` is not yet computed when `mail` is evaluated, so mail comes out empty/literal or wrong. Fix: move the `uid` field above `mail` in the policy's `fields` array, keep `mail` as `{"type":"static","attributes":{"value":"$uid@corp.com"}}`. Static values cannot read identity attributes directly (map them to an earlier field first), and generator templates cannot read other create-profile fields at all. If mail itself must be unique, use the `Create Unique LDAP Attribute` generator instead. Apply via `GET /sources/v1/{sourceId}/provisioning-policies/CREATE`, reorder, validate with `scripts/check_source_config.py` (it flags static values that reference later fields), then `PUT` back.
B: Create profile attributes are evaluated in the order they appear in the provisioning policy fields, and a static Velocity value can only reference fields already computed earlier in the policy (or identity attributes). Because uid (Create Unique Account ID generator) is defined below mail, $uid is not yet resolved when mail is built, so you get a literal/empty value. Fix: move the uid field above mail in the create profile (field order in the /v3/sources/{id}/provisioning-policies/CREATE fields array), then reference it as $uid. Also note the generator may retry for uniqueness; dependent fields must come after it. Alternatively compute mail from identity attributes with a transform/generator instead of Velocity.

q: What are the main limits of attribute sync in ISC?
must: only existing correlated accounts are updated (it never creates accounts)
only attributes in Create Account mapped directly from an identity attribute
the built-in Manager attribute cannot be synced
case-sensitive; bulk sync at most 3 times per 24h per source
must_not: says attribute sync creates missing accounts
A: Attribute sync only updates existing, correlated accounts: it never creates accounts and ignores uncorrelated ones. An attribute can be synced only if it is in Create Account and mapped directly from an identity attribute (not via a transform/generator); the built-in Manager attribute cannot be synced. Comparison is case-sensitive, nulls are propagated, and multi-valued attributes need custom rules. Bulk Sync per source is limited to at most 3 full syncs per 24 hours and only when the source is healthy; failed syncs are retried up to 10 times. It may overwrite native changes on synced attributes, and attributes also changed by rules or aggregation never converge and keep retrying. Config API is experimental: `GET/PUT /sources/v1/{id}/attribute-sync-config`, `POST /sources/v1/{id}/synchronize-attributes` (header `X-SailPoint-Experimental: true`).
B: Attribute sync pushes identity attribute values to accounts on target sources when identity attributes change (configured per source in Attribute Sync, mapping identity attribute to account attribute; source must support ENABLE/provisioning, i.e. connector with sync support). Limits: it only works on direct connectors supporting provisioning (not flat-file/delimited unless via ticket/SIM); only single-valued attributes, no multi-valued; it is triggered by identity refresh when the identity attribute value changes, not periodically reconciled for arbitrary account drift; it cannot sync attributes that are account-correlation or naming attributes on some connectors (e.g. distinguishedName/AD rename require special handling); it does not apply to disabled sync when an identity is uncorrelated; and there is a global and per-source toggle. The first enablement does not mass-sync all existing differences automatically (it only syncs on change; a full sync can be run). Changes made directly on the account are overwritten at the next sync. Values must be passed via identity attributes, transforms on the account attribute aren't applied.

q: How do I schedule account and entitlement aggregation of a source through the API?
must: POST /sources/v1/{sourceId}/schedules
type ACCOUNT_AGGREGATION or GROUP_AGGREGATION
cronExpression is a Quartz cron (seconds first, ? in day-of-month or day-of-week)
A: Use the source schedules API: POST /beta/sources/{sourceId}/schedules (also v2024/v2025) with body {"type": "ACCOUNT_AGGREGATION", "cronExpression": "0 0 2 * * ?"} and separately {"type": "GROUP_AGGREGATION", "cronExpression": "..."} for entitlements. List with GET /beta/sources/{id}/schedules, get/update/delete with GET/PATCH/DELETE /beta/sources/{id}/schedules/{scheduleType}. Cron is Quartz-style (seconds first) in UTC. To run on demand rather than schedule: POST /v3/sources/{id}/load-accounts (or /beta) and POST /beta/sources/{id}/load-entitlements. Requires scope like idn:sources:manage.
B: Use `POST /sources/v1/{sourceId}/schedules` (scope `idn:sources:manage`, ORG_ADMIN/SOURCE_ADMIN/SOURCE_SUBADMIN) with body `{"type": "ACCOUNT_AGGREGATION", "cronExpression": "0 0 5,13,21 * * ?"}`, and a second call with `"type": "GROUP_AGGREGATION"` for entitlements. `cronExpression` is a Quartz cron (seconds first, `?` in day-of-month or day-of-week, days of week 1-7 = Sunday-Saturday). One schedule per type: read with `GET /sources/v1/{sourceId}/schedules[/{scheduleType}]`, change with `PATCH /sources/v1/{sourceId}/schedules/{scheduleType}` (JSON Patch, `type` immutable), remove with `DELETE .../schedules/{scheduleType}`. Times run in the VA cluster's time zone and do not follow DST. Quick Compliance sources allow at most 3 runs a day, 8 hours apart (not for Org Admins). For one-off runs use `POST /sources/v1/{id}/load-accounts` and `POST /sources/v1/{sourceId}/load-entitlements`.

q: I enabled native change detection but no Native Change triggers fire. What do I check?
must: at least one operation (ACCOUNT_CREATED/UPDATED/DELETED) and at least one attribute/entitlement must be selected
changes are detected only when an aggregation runs
triggers: Native Change Account Created/Updated/Deleted
must_not: says NCD detects changes in real time without aggregation
A: NCD only finds changes when an account aggregation runs, by comparing what it reads with what ISC stored, so check that aggregations are actually running (scheduled/full). In the config (`GET/PUT /sources/v1/{sourceId}/native-change-detection-config`) `enabled` must be true, at least one operation (`ACCOUNT_CREATED`, `ACCOUNT_UPDATED`, `ACCOUNT_DELETED`) must be selected, and at least one attribute (`allEntitlements`, `allNonEntitlementAttributes`, `selectedEntitlements`, `selectedNonEntitlementAttributes`); for Updated, the changed attribute must be a monitored one. Check the trigger subscription exists and is enabled for Native Change Account Created/Updated/Deleted, and that any JSONPath filter does not drop the events. Look for audit events Create/Update/Delete Native Change Detected to see whether detection happened. NCD is not available for Non-Employee sources, and SAML Just-in-Time sources must be configured through the API. Also, an optimized aggregation of unchanged data yields nothing to detect, and attribute sync may revert native changes.
B: Check: (1) the source's connector supports native change detection (e.g. AD, Entra, some others) and the source is direct (not delimited); (2) NCD is enabled on the source with the right operations selected (account create/update/delete) and attributes - for updates only the configured attributes (entitlements/selected attrs) generate events; (3) detection only happens during account aggregation - changes must have been made directly on the target (not by ISC provisioning, which is excluded), and an aggregation must run after the change; optimized aggregation still detects changes, but the first aggregation after enabling builds the baseline; (4) the Native Change event trigger (idn:account-native-change? 'Native Change Account Created/Updated/Deleted' triggers) has an active subscription or a workflow using it, with correct filter; (5) uncorrelated accounts may not be included. Look at subscription testing and trigger invocation status (GET /beta/trigger-invocations/status).

q: How do I update the create profile of a source via API? Can a source have several CREATE policies?
must: PUT /sources/v1/{sourceId}/provisioning-policies/CREATE (GET first, edit, PUT back)
v1 has one policy per usageType; several per usage type only with the experimental v2 API by id (subtypes)
A: The create profile is the provisioning policy with usageType CREATE: GET /v3/sources/{sourceId}/provisioning-policies/CREATE, replace it with PUT /v3/sources/{sourceId}/provisioning-policies/CREATE (full body: name, usageType, fields[] with name, transform, attributes, isRequired, type, isMultiValued), or partially update with PATCH (JSON Patch, Content-Type application/json-patch+json) e.g. op replace on /fields/2/transform. If none exists, create with POST /v3/sources/{sourceId}/provisioning-policies. There is also bulk-update POST /v3/sources/{id}/provisioning-policies/bulk-update. A source can have only one policy per usageType, so only one CREATE policy; other usage types (UPDATE, ENABLE, DISABLE, DELETE, CHANGE_PASSWORD, etc.) are separate policies.
B: The Create Account profile is the provisioning policy with `usageType: CREATE`: read it with `GET /sources/v1/{sourceId}/provisioning-policies/CREATE`, edit, and `PUT` the whole object back to the same path (or `PATCH` with JSON Patch); create one with `POST /sources/v1/{sourceId}/provisioning-policies`, several at once with `POST .../provisioning-policies/bulk-update`. Body: `name`, `description`, `usageType`, `fields[]` (each with `name` case-sensitive account attribute, `type` string/int/long/date/boolean/secret, `isRequired`, `isMultiValued`, `transform`, `attributes`); field order matters. In v1 there is one policy per usage type, so a source cannot have several CREATE policies. Several policies per usage type exist only through the experimental v2 API by id, `/sources/v2/{sourceId}/provisioning-policies[/{id}]` (header `X-SailPoint-Experimental: true`), used for source subtypes / machine accounts (`subtypeId`, `CREATE_MACHINE_ACCOUNT`). Validate first with `scripts/check_source_config.py`.

q: How can I list uncorrelated accounts of a source via API and correlate them in bulk?
must: GET /accounts/v1 with filters sourceId eq "..." and uncorrelated eq true
bulk manual correlation: correlation file (userName column) uploaded via UI or POST /sources/v1/{id}/load-uncorrelated-accounts
manual links are flagged manuallyCorrelated=true and survive unoptimized aggregation
must_not: says identity search @accounts finds uncorrelated accounts
A: List uncorrelated accounts with GET /v3/accounts?filters=sourceId eq "<sourceId>" and uncorrelated eq true (paginate with limit up to 250 and offset, count=true for total). Alternatively use search for accounts. To correlate, call PUT /v3/accounts/{accountId} with body {"identityId": "<identityId>"} for each account (there is no single bulk correlate endpoint in v3; loop with rate-limit handling, ~100 req/10s). In the UI you can bulk correlate via Uncorrelated Accounts by uploading a CSV correlation file (account ID/name to identity). Better long-term: fix correlation config and run an unoptimized aggregation (disableOptimization=true) so ISC correlates them automatically.
B: List them with `GET /accounts/v1?filters=sourceId eq "<sourceId>" and uncorrelated eq true` (page with `limit`/`offset`); identity search does not see uncorrelated accounts. In the UI there is also Account Management > Uncorrelated Accounts and the Uncorrelated Accounts report (Admin > Global > Reports). To correlate in bulk, download the correlation file (Uncorrelated Accounts > Download Correlation File), fill the target identity's account ID in `userName`, and upload it with `POST /sources/v1/{id}/load-uncorrelated-accounts` (`multipart/form-data`, field `file`, scope `idn:sources:manage`, ORG_ADMIN; returns 202 with a task). Those links are stored as `manuallyCorrelated=true` and are not undone by unoptimized aggregation; up to 100 accounts per identity. If the cause is a correlation config problem, fix the config and run `load-accounts` with `disableOptimization=true` instead.

q: A colleague wants to add PROVISIONING to the features array of our SailPoint-supported JDBC source to enable provisioning. Good idea?
must: SailPoint advises not to modify the features array for SailPoint-supported connectors (can cause unsupportable configuration errors)
enable provisioning through the connector's supported configuration instead
A: No. The `features` array describes what the connector implements (`PROVISIONING` means the connector can read and write accounts and implements provision()); the API spec warns that modifying it may cause unsupportable source configuration errors and recommends not modifying it for SailPoint-supported connectors. Adding the flag does not add write capability; it can break the source. Enable provisioning through the supported connector configuration instead (for JDBC, the connector's provisioning settings/scripts or JDBC provisioning connector rules, see isc-rules), plus a Create Account profile (`provisioning-policies/CREATE`). The skill's checker flags unknown features but the rule is: do not touch `features` on SailPoint-supported connectors.
B: No. The features array describes what the connector actually implements; for SailPoint-supported connectors it is set by the connector/type and editing it doesn't add capability, it can cause failures or unexpected behavior (ISC would try to send provisioning plans the connector configuration isn't set up for), and it is an unsupported configuration. For JDBC, provisioning is implemented through JDBC Provision rules (connector rule JDBCProvision, uploaded via the connector rules API /beta/connector-rules and referenced in the source's connectorAttributes, e.g. provisioning rule) and enabling provisioning in the source config; once configured properly the source supports provisioning. Changing features via PATCH /v3/sources/{id} should be reserved for cases documented by SailPoint (e.g. removing features to disable behavior, or some flat-file/custom SaaS connectors), and done with care.
